data_json.rule: être in the present tense: je suis, tu es, il/elle est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils/elles sont
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct form of 'être' for 'nous'.
data_json.explanation: 'Nous' takes 'sommes'. The full conjugation of être is: je suis, tu es, il/elle est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils/elles sont.

data_json.rule: être in the present tense: je suis, tu es, il/elle est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils/elles sont
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct form of 'être' for 'ils'.
data_json.explanation: 'Ils' and 'elles' both take 'sont'. Remember: ils/elles → sont.

data_json.rule: avoir in the present tense: j'ai, tu as, il/elle a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct form of 'avoir' for 'nous'.
data_json.explanation: 'Nous' takes 'avons'. The full conjugation of avoir is: j'ai, tu as, il/elle a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont.

breakdown: un chien is the direct object

data_json.rule: avoir in the present tense: j'ai, tu as, il/elle a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct form of 'avoir' for 'ils'.
data_json.explanation: 'Ils/elles' takes 'ont'. Do not confuse 'ont' (have) with 'on' (one/we) which takes 'a'.

data_json.rule: Regular -er verbs drop -er and add: -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct present-tense form of 'parler' for 'nous'.
data_json.explanation: For -er verbs, remove -er then add -ons for nous. parler → parl- + ons = parlons.

data_json.rule: Regular -er verbs drop -er and add: -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct present-tense form of 'manger' for 'ils'.
data_json.explanation: For -er verbs, remove -er then add -ent for ils/elles. manger → mange- + nt = mangent. The -e is kept before -nt for pronunciation.

breakdown: ils → + nt → mangent (keeps -e- for soft g)

data_json.rule: faire (to do/make) is irregular: je fais, tu fais, il fait, nous faisons, vous faites, ils font
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct form of 'faire' for 'vous'.
data_json.explanation: 'Vous faites' is irregular — not 'faisez'. This is one of only two -er verbs with an irregular vous form (the other is être → êtes).

data_json.rule: aller (to go) is irregular: je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct form of 'aller' for 'ils'.
data_json.explanation: 'Ils vont' — aller is highly irregular in the present tense. The stem changes completely: all- for nous/vous but v- for other forms.

breakdown: à + le = au, à + la = à la, à + l' = à l'

data_json.rule: prendre is irregular: je prends, tu prends, il prend, nous prenons, vous prenez, ils prennent
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct form of 'prendre' for 'ils'.
data_json.explanation: 'Ils prennent' — note the double -nn- in the ils/elles form. This pattern applies to compounds: apprendre, comprendre, surprendre.

breakdown: same pattern: ils apprennent, ils comprennent

data_json.rule: vouloir is irregular: je veux, tu veux, il veut, nous voulons, vous voulez, ils veulent
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct form of 'vouloir' for 'je'.
data_json.explanation: 'Je veux' — vouloir has a stem change: voul- for nous/vous, veuil- (written veu-) for other persons. Do not say 'je voudrais' for present tense fact; that is conditional (I would like).

breakdown: contrast: je voudrais (I would like) = polite conditional

data_json.rule: Basic negation: place 'ne' before the verb and 'pas' after it. Ne becomes n' before a vowel.
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct negative form of 'parle' for 'il ne ___ français'.
data_json.explanation: Negation wraps the verb: ne + verb + pas. 'Il ne parle pas français.' In spoken French, 'ne' is often dropped, but write it in formal contexts.

breakdown: ne ... pas wraps the conjugated verb

data_json.rule: ne...jamais (never) negates frequency. Structure mirrors ne...pas: ne + verb + jamais.
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct phrase for 'he never eats meat': 'il ___ de viande'.
data_json.explanation: ne...jamais = never. Like ne...pas, jamais follows the verb. After negation, un/une/du/de la/des → de: il ne mange jamais de viande.

examples.fr: Il ne mange jamais de viande.

data_json.rule: ne...plus (no longer/no more) indicates something that used to be true but is not now.
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct phrase meaning 'he no longer smokes': 'il ___'.
data_json.explanation: ne...plus wraps the conjugated verb just like ne...pas. It implies a change from a past state: he used to smoke, but doesn't anymore.

breakdown: implies contrast with a past state

data_json.rule: Intonation question: raise pitch at the end of a declarative sentence to form a yes/no question.
data_json.prompt: Which sentence is a correct intonation question meaning 'Do you speak French?'
data_json.explanation: Intonation questions keep SVO order and raise pitch. They are common in spoken French. All three — intonation, est-ce que, and inversion — are grammatically correct.

breakdown: Question conveyed by rising intonation or '?'

data_json.rule: est-ce que + subject + verb forms a question without changing word order.
data_json.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct 'est-ce que' question for 'Are you coming?'
data_json.explanation: est-ce que + normal SVO word order. Est-ce que becomes est-ce qu' before a vowel: Est-ce qu'il vient ?

data_json.rule: Inversion questions: verb-subject hyphenated. If il/elle verb ends in vowel, insert -t- for euphony.
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct inversion question: 'Does he speak French?'
data_json.explanation: When the verb ends in -e and the subject is il/elle/on, insert -t- between verb and pronoun for euphony: parle → parle-t-il. Without -t- would be 'parle-il' which is hard to pronounce.

breakdown: verb-t-pronoun when verb ends in vowel

data_json.rule: Passé composé with avoir: subject + avoir (present) + past participle. -er verbs → -é, -ir verbs → -i, -re verbs → -u.
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct passé composé of 'manger' for 'je'.
data_json.explanation: Passé composé = avoir/être (present) + past participle. For manger: auxiliaire avoir + past participle mangé (remove -er, add -é).

breakdown: no agreement with avoir (unless object precedes)

data_json.rule: Passé composé with être: 17 verbs (DR & MRS VAN DER TRAMP) + reflexives use être; past participle agrees with subject.
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct passé composé of 'aller' for 'elle'.
data_json.explanation: Aller uses être as auxiliary. The past participle (allé) must agree with the subject: elle → allée (add -e). If subject were il → allé, ils → allés, elles → allées.

data_json.rule: With avoir, the past participle agrees with a preceding direct object, not the subject.
data_json.prompt: Choose the sentence with correct past participle agreement: '___ sont belles.'
data_json.explanation: When a direct object precedes the verb with avoir, the past participle agrees with it. 'fleurs' is feminine plural, so achetées (add -es). This is called l'accord du participe passé.

examples.fr: Les fleurs qu'il a achetées sont belles.
examples.en: The flowers he bought are beautiful.
breakdown: preceding direct object → past participle agrees: achetées

data_json.rule: Imparfait formation: take the nous present tense stem + endings: -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient.
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct imparfait form of 'parler' for 'je'.
data_json.explanation: Imparfait stem = nous present minus -ons: parlons → parl-. Add -ais for je: parlais. Être is the only exception: stem is ét- (from étions).

examples.fr: Quand j'étais enfant, je parlais espagnol.
examples.en: When I was a child, I spoke Spanish.

data_json.rule: Imparfait expresses habitual past actions or background states; passé composé expresses completed events.
mc_options: Il lisait quand le téléphone a sonné.
Il lisait quand le téléphone sonnait.
Il a lu quand le téléphone a sonné.
Il lisait quand le téléphone sonner.
Il a lu quand le téléphone sonnait.
Il lisait quand le téléphone est sonné.
data_json.correct_answer: Il lisait quand le téléphone a sonné.
data_json.prompt: Choose the sentence that correctly contrasts imparfait (background) and passé composé (event).
data_json.explanation: Lisait (imparfait) = ongoing background action. A sonné (passé composé) = sudden completed event that interrupted it. The classic signal: imparfait for 'was doing', passé composé for 'did/happened'.

examples.fr: Il lisait quand le téléphone a sonné.
examples.en: He was reading when the phone rang.
breakdown: a sonné = punctual event that interrupted (passé composé)

data_json.rule: French nouns are either masculine or feminine. Definite articles: le (masc.), la (fem.), l' (before vowel/h), les (plural).
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct definite article for 'livre' (book), which is masculine.
data_json.explanation: 'Livre' is masculine, so it takes 'le'. There is no reliable rule for gender — it must be memorised with each noun. Tip: learn 'le livre', 'la table' not just 'livre', 'table'.

examples.fr: Le livre est sur la table.
examples.en: The book is on the table.

data_json.rule: Adjectives agree in gender and number with the noun. Most add -e for feminine, -s for plural, -es for feminine plural.
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct form of 'grand' to describe 'une maison' (feminine singular).
data_json.explanation: Feminine singular adjectives add -e to the masculine base: grand → grande. If the masculine already ends in -e (rouge, jaune), no extra -e is added.

data_json.rule: Some adjectives have irregular feminine forms: beau → belle, nouveau → nouvelle, vieux → vieille, blanc → blanche.
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct feminine singular form of 'beau'.
data_json.explanation: Beau → belle (feminine). Before a masculine noun starting with a vowel, use the special form 'bel': un bel homme. Plural: beaux (masc.), belles (fem.).

data_json.rule: Direct object pronouns replace the direct object: me, te, le/la, nous, vous, les. They go before the conjugated verb.
data_json.prompt: Replace 'le garçon' with a pronoun: 'Je vois le garçon.' → ?
data_json.explanation: Direct object pronouns precede the verb. 'Le garçon' is masculine singular, so le → 'Je le vois.' Before a vowel, le/la elide to l': 'Je l'entends.'

examples.fr: Je le vois. / Je la vois.
examples.en: I see him. / I see her.
breakdown: direct object pronoun goes before the verb
le = masc., la = fem., les = plural

data_json.rule: Indirect object pronouns replace à + person: me, te, lui, nous, vous, leur. They also precede the verb.
data_json.prompt: Replace 'à Marie' with an indirect object pronoun: 'Je parle à Marie.' → ?
data_json.explanation: 'À Marie' (indirect object) → lui. Note: lui = him OR her for indirect objects, unlike direct objects (le/la). Do not confuse lui (indirect) with lui (stressed/disjunctive pronoun).

examples.fr: Je lui parle. (à Marie ou à Paul)
breakdown: lui replaces both à + masculine and à + feminine person

data_json.rule: Relative clause with 'qui': qui is the subject of the relative clause (who/that). It can refer to people or things.
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun: 'L'homme ___ parle est mon père.'
data_json.explanation: 'Qui' is the subject of the relative clause: 'l'homme parle' → l'homme qui parle. Use qui when the relative pronoun is the subject of its clause. Use que when it is the object.

examples.fr: L'homme qui parle est mon père.
examples.en: The man who is speaking is my father.

data_json.rule: Relative clause with 'que': que is the direct object of the relative clause (whom/that). It elides to qu' before a vowel.
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun: 'Le livre ___ tu lis est intéressant.'
data_json.explanation: 'Que' is the object: 'tu lis le livre' → 'le livre que tu lis'. Notice that a subject (tu) follows que. If a verb follows directly, use qui.

examples.fr: Le livre que tu lis est intéressant.
examples.en: The book (that) you are reading is interesting.
breakdown: que = direct object of relative clause

data_json.rule: 'dont' replaces de + noun in a relative clause (whose, of which, about which).
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun: 'C'est le film ___ je t'ai parlé.'
data_json.explanation: 'Parler de quelque chose' → dont replaces 'de ce film'. Dont is used when the relative pronoun replaces de + noun. Also used for possession: 'l'homme dont la femme est médecin'.

examples.fr: C'est le film dont je t'ai parlé.
examples.en: That's the film I told you about.

data_json.rule: Futur simple: add endings to the infinitive (-ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont). For -re verbs, drop final -e first.
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct futur simple of 'parler' for 'je'.
data_json.explanation: Futur simple = infinitive + endings. parler + -ai = parlerai. Note: -rais (with s) is the conditional — easy to confuse with -rai (futur, no s).

examples.en: Tomorrow I will speak to the director.
breakdown: do not drop -er before adding ending for -er verbs

data_json.rule: Several verbs have irregular futur stems: être → ser-, avoir → aur-, aller → ir-, faire → fer-, vouloir → voudr-, pouvoir → pourr-.
data_json.prompt: Choose the correct futur simple of 'être' for 'ils'.
data_json.explanation: Être has the irregular stem 'ser-'. Add -ont for ils: seront. Key irregular stems: être→ser, avoir→aur, aller→ir, faire→fer, pouvoir→pourr, vouloir→voudr, venir→viendr.
